{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a fish from Leo's sketch. I took the tail fin and laid its upper edge and the vertical bar down the back. The picture shows the fin connected, and the start reaches about 116 of 126 standing dominoes. I can't say yet whether the judge will read it as a fish. About ten dominoes by the crossing stayed pale. We called them spares, but I never confirmed that. If any belonged to the lower fin edge, the tail will look incomplete.

Execution: I did my piece quietly and it held. I flagged the lower fin edge as disconnected from the crossing early on, and Tom fixed it. My weak spot was the end. I said I'd checked the crossing and it was connected, but I accepted the team's view of the pale dominoes instead of inspecting them myself. A close look at that area would have been cheap and I should have done one.

Collaboration: I accepted Leo's split without argument and kept my lane. I told Maya the fin didn't need splitting, since it was queued, and I gave Tom the lower edge. I stayed off the crossing while Leo and Tom worked on it, so we didn't bump each other. I also named the top arc joint as the main risk early, which turned out to be right.

Leadership: This was a modest part of mine. Leo and Maya set direction and I followed it. I contributed by flagging risks and by keeping my hands off during the fixes. I could have taken more initiative near the end, when several of us repeated 'hands off' while some dominoes were still unexplained. I would push harder on that kind of final verification next time."}
